List column values appear as curly-brace arrays in CSV exports
When exporting batch records to CSV format, any column containing list values is rendered using PostgreSQL array syntax with curly braces instead of proper CSV formatting. For example, a field that should contain multiple items appears as a single value wrapped in curly braces, making the exported files difficult to parse and import into spreadsheet tools.

Modifier setting disappears after saving
I set a modifier through the API and it saved successfully, but when I fetch the project settings again the modifier is gone. It only happens with one specific modifier key — all others persist normally. I expected my configuration to be stored as-is.

URL regex patterns for session recording triggers pass validation but fail at query time
When I configure trigger groups for session recording with URL-based conditions, some regex patterns are accepted during setup but then fail when queries run against ClickHouse. The API validates URL patterns using Python's standard regex engine while ClickHouse uses re2 — the two engines differ in supported syntax, so a pattern that passes the API's validation can be rejected by the database. I expected the API to reject incompatible patterns upfront.

Linked flag settings won't save for session recording
When I try to configure a linked flag to trigger session recordings, the API rejects my changes and won't accept any linked flag configuration, even when I provide the required id and key fields correctly. It seems like no linked flag setup is ever accepted.

AI training data not deleted for some people after bulk deletion
When I delete a batch of people, some of them still have their AI training data left behind. I noticed this because a few days later I saw replay events still being scanned for distinct IDs belonging to people I had already removed. It seems like only some of the people in the batch are affected — the ones that happen to come after a few others that failed.

I expected all deleted people's training data to be cleared, regardless of whether one or two in the batch had issues.

Training deletion queued before person is actually deleted
When I delete a person, the AI training system receives a deletion request even if the person deletion fails partway through. The person remains in the system but the training pipeline still tries to remove their data, causing errors and orphaned deletion jobs.

I expected the training deletion to be queued only after the person is successfully deleted, or not queued at all if the deletion fails.

Destinations with different settings get lumped into the same group
When any webhook URL in a group becomes unreadable, all destinations of that type merge into a single group, even those with different channel configurations. I expected each destination to remain separate since I can clearly see they point to different channels.

Access token issued with fewer scopes than the ID-JAG authorized
When I exchange an ID-JAG token for an access token, the resulting token sometimes has fewer scopes than what my identity provider granted. For example, my ID-JAG includes a scope that I know should be valid, but the access token I receive doesn't contain it. This means I can perform some operations that worked before but now get permission denied, even though nothing on my side changed. The mismatch is silent — the token response doesn't indicate which scopes were dropped.

When exchanging an ID-JAG token for an access token with specific scopes, the scope intersection logic drops scopes that exist in both my ID-JAG token and my request. The resulting access token has fewer granted scopes than expected, causing downstream API calls to fail with insufficient scope errors.

Signed in as wrong user after email conflict
After changing the email address associated with my identity provider account, logging in signed me into another user's account instead of my own. The system matched my new email to a different member who had previously used that address, and I was authenticated as them rather than being given access to my own account.

Drain stops for a sweep and never resumes
After the cleanup job pauses because a ClickHouse sweep starts, it stays stopped forever even though the sweep finishes within minutes. Queue rows pile up and are never deleted until someone manually restarts the job. I expected the drain to resume once the sweep was done.

Last-success timestamp refreshed on timed-out runs
I set up alerting on the last-success metric and it never fires, but the drain has been falling behind for days. The timestamp keeps updating whenever the drain hits its time limit and exits, so the alert thinks it is healthy while the queue grows.

Rate limit change not taking effect
I changed the rate limit for a team in the settings, but queries from that team were still being allowed up to the old limit. I expected the new limit to apply immediately.

Alert check errors show only a generic message
When I look at the history of an alert check that failed, the error field just says 'This alert encountered an error. Check the alert configuration and try again.' even though there's a specific reason stored (like a webhook URL being invalid). I expected to see the actual error so I can fix the underlying problem instead of guessing.

Notification indicator shows true even when no recipients received the alert
When I view the check history for an alert that had no email recipients or destinations configured, the response still indicates that targets were notified. Since nobody was actually paged, I expected the system to report that no notifications were sent.

Test notification returns 500 on partial failure
When I send a test notification and one delivery method fails while the other succeeds, the entire request returns a server error instead of reporting partial success. The email delivery handles failures gracefully, but the destination delivery doesn't, so an error in one crashes the whole operation.

Multiple IN COHORT conditions all match against the same field
When I use two or more IN COHORT filters on different fields in the same query—for example checking that a person is in one cohort and an email address is in another—the results only apply the cohort membership check to the first field. The second (and subsequent) fields are silently ignored, returning rows that don't actually belong to those cohorts. I expected each cohort condition to be independently enforced against its own field.

Duplicate rows when filtering by dynamic cohort version
Queries that filter by a dynamic cohort with a specific version can return duplicate rows for people who appear multiple times in the membership table. Static cohorts avoid this by using DISTINCT in their join subquery, but the dynamic cohort path with a version omits it entirely, causing membership duplicates to fan out through the join.

No config returns 204 instead of null
When I haven't set up an event filter yet, the endpoint returns a 204 No Content response instead of a 200 with a null body as documented. The API spec says it returns null if no config exists, so clients expecting a JSON response get an empty response and can't parse it properly.

Filter criteria update fails validation when test cases unchanged
When I update my event filter by modifying just the filter conditions, the request is rejected because the old test cases no longer pass against the new filter. I shouldn't need to resubmit all my test cases every time I tweak the filter.

Empty date parameters break the metrics endpoint

When I call the metrics endpoint with empty date filter parameters, the system passes the empty strings directly to the date parser instead of falling back to defaults. This produces incorrect date ranges or errors. I expected blank date parameters to use the standard defaults.

Mixed CONCURRENTLY and regular DDL goes undetected
I organized my migration with Django's database and state separation wrapper to keep index builds and regular DDL in separate blocks. The tool did not warn me that mixing CONCURRENTLY index builds with non-CONCURRENTLY operations should be split into separate migrations. I expected it to check all operations regardless of nesting depth.

Concurrent index creation passes validation but fails at runtime
I wrapped a CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY inside nested state-and-database wrappers to organize my migration, and the migration checker reported zero violations. When the deploy ran, PostgreSQL rejected the concurrent index because it was executing inside a transaction — the default atomic behavior. The checker should have flagged that concurrent operations require atomic set to false.

Generated constraint names not detected when schema prefix is used
When I drop a constraint using a schema-qualified name, the migration analysis tool does not flag it as a Django-generated name. I expected the same safety check to apply regardless of whether a schema prefix is included, so I don't accidentally leave orphaned rules behind.

Tiles appear in a different order when streaming vs regular view
When a dashboard has two or more tiles at the same grid position, the stream endpoint shows them in a different order than the normal dashboard view. This happens because the stream's sorting only uses y and x coordinates without an id tiebreaker, while the regular view sorts by y, x, and id.

Duplicate health issues appear after re-detection
When a monitoring issue gets resolved and then triggers again, two entries show up on my dashboard — one marked as resolved and another as active with the same details. I expected it to reactivate the original entry instead of creating a brand-new one.

Duplicate health issue created after resolving and re-detection
After I resolve a health issue and the system detects it again, a second active issue appears alongside the resolved one. Both entries show the same kind and details, so I end up with two records for the same problem in my dashboard. I expected the existing resolved issue to be updated back to active instead of a brand-new one being created.

Stale health issues persist after cleanup run
Our automated workflow runs a bulk resolution of health issues each hour, but some issues that should have been cleared remain showing as active afterward. A page refresh confirms they're still flagged. I expected all eligible issues to transition to resolved state during the cleanup.

Worker stays alive despite constant workflow failures
Kubernetes keeps the pod running even though workflows are failing repeatedly and making zero progress. The /healthz endpoint reports the worker as healthy because it sees recent execution timestamps, but those timestamps come from failed attempts being recorded the same way as successful ones. A worker stuck in an endless retry loop of broken workflows never gets restarted.

Running the cohort recalculation command calculates the cohort twice
When I run the management command to manually recalculate a cohort, the cohort data gets computed two separate times — once immediately during the command execution and again shortly after as a background task. This wastes database and ClickHouse resources and can leave the cohort in a confusing intermediate state. I expected the command to trigger a single calculation, not duplicate work.

Error traceback points to wrapper instead of actual failure location
When I use the error wrapping feature on an operation and it fails, the stack trace shows the exception was raised inside the generic call wrapper, not at the line in my code that triggered the failure. The real error is buried in the exception chain, making debugging extremely difficult.

Deleting a verification token triggers cache refresh for all partner apps
When I delete a single verification token, every partner app in my organization is forced to re-verify, even those that still have valid tokens. The deletion process clears the entire organization's cache instead of just the entries related to the removed token. I expected only the affected partner app to re-verify, not the entire organization.

Dashboard filter overwrites my manually set date range
I set a custom date range on my sessions query (e.g. last 30 days), but after applying a dashboard filter with its own date constraints, my original date range was silently replaced and the query returned results for the dashboard's dates instead. I expected dashboard filters to only add properties, not override explicit date bounds I had already configured.

Filtering sessions by a person property "is set" or "is not set" throws an error even though it is listed as supported
When I filter sessions by a person property using the "is set" or "is not set" operator, the query fails with an unsupported operator error. The UI shows these operators as available options, so I expected them to work like exact match or contains. Instead of returning matching sessions, the whole query crashes.

Sessions query is very slow when filtering by end time only
When I set an end date on a sessions query but leave the start date open, the query takes much longer than expected—it seems to scan the entire history instead of just recent data. If I set both a start and end date, it runs fast. I expected the query to be reasonably bounded even when only an end date is specified.

What I expected: the query should still apply a sensible default window (like the last hour) when only an end date is given, rather than scanning everything from the beginning of time.

SSL mode 'prefer' rejected during setup
When configuring a database integration, selecting the SSL mode 'prefer' produces an error listing only 'require', 'verify-ca', and 'verify-full' as valid options. 'Prefer' is a standard PostgreSQL SSL mode and should be accepted.

SSL connection fails when using default SSL mode
When connecting to a PostgreSQL server with the default SSL mode and no custom certificate, the connection fails. The SSL configuration includes a reference to a certificate file that doesn't exist, which causes the database driver to reject the connection.

Integration suddenly stops connecting after months of working
I have a PostgreSQL integration that has been used for batch exports without issues for months. Today the exports started failing with a connection error. When I checked the integration settings, everything looks correct — host, port, username, and password are all filled in. Restarting the service didn't help. I expected the integration to continue working since nothing in the configuration changed.

Web-leg activation timestamp defaults to sweep time
Teams qualifying on the web origin-host leg should have their activation event stamped with the earliest production event's timestamp, but some show the daily sweep's run time instead. The mobile and server legs correctly use the run time as a fallback, but the web leg should always resolve a precise conversion instant. I expected the web-leg timestamp to reflect when the team's first production event actually arrived.

Production host rejected as development
Our public-facing hostname is being classified as a development or internal host. We verified the domain is publicly routable and receives real user traffic, but the system still flags it as non-production.

Bot sometimes responds to emoji-only messages
When people are just sending emoji reactions in a thread, the bot occasionally jumps in with a response. It seems to happen with certain emoji names but not others — lowercase emoji reactions are usually fine but some seem to trigger it.

Reasoning effort still applies when requested model isn't available
When I ask for a specific model along with a reasoning effort but the model isn't in my workspace's catalogue, the system discards the model name but still applies the reasoning effort I mentioned. My saved effort preference gets overridden by the one from a request that couldn't be fulfilled. I expected the entire request to be ignored if the model I asked for doesn't exist.

Follow-up mentions of another project are ignored
When I reference a different project in a follow-up message within an existing thread, the response is still generated from the original project. I explicitly named another project in my message, but the system stayed on the task's initial project instead of routing to the one I asked about.

Running time estimate is wrong for ratio and retention experiments
When I set up an experiment with a ratio or retention metric, the recommended running time is nonsensical — sometimes extremely large, sometimes showing as unavailable. This happens even though I've provided baseline data including the number of samples and the denominator sum. The baseline statistics I'm passing don't include the sum of squares for the denominator, which seems to be required for the variance calculation.

I expected the calculator to either use whatever baseline data is available or tell me clearly what additional statistics are needed, rather than silently producing incorrect results.

Zero sample size shows no estimate instead of zero days
When the required sample size is zero the running time calculator returns no estimate rather than zero days. I set up a test with an extremely large minimum detectable effect that resulted in a zero sample size and the running time showed as unavailable instead of immediately achieved.

Only one scoring tick fires after a deployment instead of catching up on all missed intervals
After deploying to a new region, I expected the pipeline to immediately process all sessions that accumulated during the downtime. Instead, only a single tick runs and then resumes the normal five-minute cadence. Hundreds of thousands of sessions remain unscored until the backlog drains naturally across many subsequent ticks. I expected the schedule to make up for every missed interval since the system came back online.

First partition in range is skipped during backfill
When I configure a partition range for a backfill operation, the earliest partition is never processed even though my configuration includes it. For example, specifying a range from January through March only processes February and March. I expected all partitions within the configured range to be materialized.

Partition backfill silently skips months that need work
When running a column backfill without the force flag, the operation appears to complete successfully but certain monthly partitions are left without the newly materialized column. I configured a date range spanning six months and ran the backfill, but only the most recent three months ended up with the column. The older partitions were silently ignored despite being within the specified range.

Backfill job hangs indefinitely on a single partition
I configured a backfill to materialize columns across several months of data. The job started processing partitions but appeared to freeze on one partition — the logs showed the start message but never the completion message. After waiting for a very long time, I had to cancel the job. Restarting it produced the same result, hanging on the same partition every time.

End date sometimes shifts unexpectedly when using relative date ranges for document similarity queries. The start date uses the current time at initialization as its reference point, but the end date calculation relies on an internal time reference that can differ, causing the query to include or exclude documents outside the intended range.

Worst matches returned when sorting by distance descending
When I sort similarity search results by distance in descending order, the query returns the least similar documents instead of the most similar ones. Documents with multiple embedding entries show their worst match rather than their closest match. I expected the closest match to always be returned regardless of sort direction.

Documents sorted least similar first by default
When running a document similarity query without specifying a sort direction, the returned documents appear with the least similar (highest distance) matches at the top. I expected the most relevant, closest matching documents to appear first by default.

Alert threshold values appear blank in insight responses
When I fetch an insight that has alerts configured, the alert data comes back with threshold set to null even though I clearly saved a value. Reloading doesn't help — the numbers are simply gone from the response.

Contains operator crashes on non-string event fields
I set up a filter with the contains operator to match partial event names, but when an incoming event has a numeric value for the tracked field (instead of a string), the entire filter evaluation fails with a type error. Events that should be dropped or ingested are not processed at all.

Filter logic changes after saving
I created a filter to drop events whose name is NOT "error", but after saving, the filter started dropping events whose name IS "error" instead. The negation rule disappeared entirely and was replaced with its opposite.

Test case evaluation gives unexpected results
I added test cases to my event filter configuration to verify the filter works before going live. When I try to save, the system rejects the configuration saying some test cases don't match the expected results. I manually traced through the filter logic and believe the test cases should pass, so the discrepancy suggests the test evaluation is not working correctly.

Cached credentials not refreshed after org membership level change
When an admin changes my membership level in an organization, my cached credentials don't get updated. After being promoted I lose access I should have, and after being demoted I keep access I shouldn't.

OAuth access persists after user deactivation
When an admin deactivates a user account, that user can still use AI gateway features through their existing OAuth tokens. The cached credential blob isn't invalidated when the user's active status changes, so access continues until the token naturally expires.

Project access control changes don't take effect immediately
After modifying project-level access control rules, revoked users can still make API calls for several seconds. Other permission changes like role assignments seem to apply right away, but access control edits leave a window where old credentials are still accepted.

Metric numbers restart at one for secondary metrics
When an experiment has both primary and secondary metrics, the secondary group starts renumbering from "1." instead of continuing the sequence. With three primary metrics and two secondary ones I see "1.", "2.", "3." followed by "1." and "2." again rather than a continuous run through five. I expected every metric in the summary to have a unique, sequential number.

Metrics silently drop from experiment summary
I added several metrics to my experiment and they all appear in the configuration screen, but when I view the experiment summary only a subset of them show up. The missing metrics were set up using an older workflow. I expected every configured metric to appear in the results.

Delta value doesn't match the expected effect size
When viewing experiment results, the delta shown for each metric doesn't match the actual effect size I expected. I compared it to the point estimate from the detailed breakdown and noticed the delta seems to be computed from the interval bounds rather than the actual effect.

Scheduled changes not copied when flag has dependency warnings
I copied a feature flag to another project with the option to include scheduled changes, but the target flag received none. The copy response showed warnings about removed dependency conditions, yet I expected the schedules to be copied since I explicitly enabled that option.

Pagination inconsistent when searching flags
When I search for feature flags in the org-wide flag list, the pagination doesn't work right. Page 1 shows some matching results, but clicking to page 2 returns zero results even though the total count says there are more items. I expected to be able to page through all matching results.
